The length of the growing season in any given region refers to the number of days when plant growth takes place. The growing season often determines which crops can be grown in an area. Depending on the region and the climate, the growing season is influenced by air temperatures, frost days, rainfall, or daylight hours. For this feature, the length of the growing season is defined as the period of time between the last frost of spring and the first frost of fall. As the climate warms and growing seasons generally grow longer, Changes in the length of the growing season can have both positive and negative effects on agriculture, as the Length of Growing Season indicator explains in more detail.
